answer: Sequential VDF puzzles impose an evaluation lag, forcing each Sybil candidate to bridge an ordered computation whose zero-knowledge proof cannot be parallelized; honest agents stake collateral, and forged identities caught at the reef of verification trigger slashing, rendering expected attack utility negative since penalty exceeds marginal Sybil gain. Because that delay resists amortization, adversary cost scales with node count, yielding a Nash equilibrium where truthful attestation dominates and the raven of consensus merely verifies proofs.
